title: De novo designed proteins modulate GPCR signalling in the dopamine D1 receptor
summary: Researchers designed four protein exoframe modulators targeting the transmembrane region of the dopamine D1 receptor. Structural studies and functional assays showed agonist-positive, negative and biased allosteric modulation; an agonist-positive modulator restored activity in loss-of-function receptor mutants. The journal abstract supports these receptor-level experiments, rather than a clinical treatment claim.
ai_technology: Computational de novo protein design (AI-based protein design pipeline)
organization: Zhejiang University; Soochow University; Hangzhou Medical College

evidence.tested: Structural and functional investigation of four designed modulators of the D1 receptor, including rescue of loss-of-function mutants.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to abstract, online date and affiliations. Therapeutic efficacy in patients is not established by these receptor experiments.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning, hallucination-like protein-design workflow used structural prompts to generate transmembrane binding modes.
